slides.0.title: Viticulture and climate: own roots, water and hazards
slides.0.subtitle: Chile's strengths and fragilities are favourite Diploma essay material
slides.1.title: Vineyards without phylloxera
slides.1.highlights.0.title: Natural quarantine
slides.1.highlights.0.content: Wine With Seth describes a "natural quarantine": the Atacama Desert to the north, the Pacific to the west, the Andes to the east and a cold southern region; controls on imported plant material add protection
slides.1.highlights.1.title: Mostly own-rooted
slides.1.highlights.1.content: Most Chilean vines grow ungrafted on their own roots, saving the cost of grafting. That deeper roots add complexity is a producer claim, not established fact
slides.1.highlights.2.title: Exceptions and caveats
slides.1.highlights.2.content: Casablanca must be grafted onto nematode-resistant rootstocks, and phylloxera-free is not disease-free: downy mildew, powdery mildew and verticillium wilt occur. Sources vary on the phylloxera date (1870 or the 1870s), so we do not compare them
slides.1.content: A Diploma answer pairs the advantage with the caveat: own-rooted vines are a gift of history and geography, not a guarantee.
slides.2.title: Drought and water
slides.2.highlights.0.title: Irrigation depends on snowmelt
slides.2.highlights.0.content: The Drinks Business (2023): Chilean vineyard irrigation depends on Andean snowmelt
slides.2.highlights.1.title: Falling rainfall
slides.2.highlights.1.content: Errázuriz's Baettig said Santiago's rainfall fell from 400 mm to 280 mm, and January to July 2021 was about 50% below average. Concha y Toro's Papa said the main issue is water, not temperature
slides.2.highlights.2.title: Shifting zones and sourcing
slides.2.highlights.2.content: The article reports some Casablanca producers leaving for lack of water and water limits on new plantings in Limarí; Concha y Toro has been shifting sourcing toward Maule for about twenty years, and Maipo's share of Casillero del Diablo Cabernet fell from 33% to 10%
slides.2.content: Drought is not only a climate issue; it redraws the regional map and brands' sourcing.
slides.3.title: Earthquakes
slides.3.highlights.0.title: 27 February 2010
slides.3.highlights.0.content: Decanter reported a magnitude 8.8 quake, the strongest in about 50 years: Maule and Bío-Bío were nearest the epicentre, Curicó and Colchagua were hit, and Aconcagua was less affected
slides.3.highlights.1.title: Cellar losses
slides.3.highlights.1.content: Torres lost about 300 smashed casks and a 100,000-litre vat cracked; Concha y Toro halted production for at least a week
slides.3.highlights.2.title: Essay angle
slides.3.highlights.2.content: Seismic risk is a fixed cost of location: cellar design, insurance and spreading sites are all discussable responses
slides.3.content: On the Pacific Ring of Fire, geological risk lives alongside the vineyards.
slides.4.title: Wildfire and sustainability
slides.4.highlights.0.title: Itata fires
slides.4.highlights.0.content: Slow Food (16 March 2023): fires in Ñuble and Bío-Bío hit Itata hardest, with an estimated 25% of Itata vineyards lost; some País vines are 200 to 250 years old. There were also major fires in 2017
slides.4.highlights.1.title: Differing accounts
slides.4.highlights.1.content: Slow Food cites pine and eucalyptus plantations among the causes; The Drinks Business gives a different burned-area figure, so we do not compare them
slides.4.highlights.2.title: Certified sustainability
slides.4.highlights.2.content: Vinetur (2025): about 80% of 2024 bottled exports came from certified sustainable wineries
slides.4.content: Old vines are wildfire's biggest casualty and the core asset of the Itata terroir argument.
How does Wine With Seth explain Chile's phylloxera-free status?
A. A natural quarantine of desert, ocean, mountains and a cold south
B. All vines are grafted onto resistant rootstock
C. It is too humid for the pest
Plus controls on imported plant material.
Which valley must be grafted onto nematode-resistant rootstock?
The exception noted by Wine With Seth.
In this lesson, "own roots give deeper, more complex wines" is?
A. A producer claim, not established fact
D. The definition of a DO
Flag it as a claim in an essay.
What did Concha y Toro's Papa call the main climate issue in Chile?
Falling rain and snowmelt dependence are central.
What was the magnitude of Chile's 27 February 2010 earthquake?
By Slow Food's estimate, how much of Itata's vineyard area was lost in the 2023 fires?
Some País vines are 200 to 250 years old.
